description: A composite group of four panels of three different kinds, all about κ-carbide formation in homogenized Fe–Mn–Al–C steel. Top-left: a TEM/HAADF micrograph filled with bright cuboidal precipitates aligned along orthogonal directions in a darker matrix; white scale bar = 50 nm. Top-right: an atom-probe tomography (APT) reconstruction of a needle-shaped specimen overlaid with an atom map; the legend lists Fe (grey), Al (cyan), Si (green) and C (dark red), scale bar = 20 nm; it shows elongated Al/Si/C-enriched, Fe-depleted cuboidal regions in a Fe-rich matrix. Bottom-left: engineering stress (MPa, ticks 0/400/800/1200) versus engineering strain (%, 0–80) with three curves — 0Si (black circles), 1Si (red triangles) and 2Si (blue squares); the 2Si curve reaches the highest level (above the 800 MPa tick) but fails at the lowest strain, the 1Si curve peaks near the 800 MPa tick at ~55% strain, and 0Si rises from near the 400 MPa level to its maximum at the highest strain (~70–80%). Bottom-right: a 3D APT reconstruction with a C colour scale, marked "Cut", scale bar = 25 nm. Together the panels show that Si-driven κ-carbide formation and solute enrichment coarsen precipitates, raising strength but strongly reducing ductility.

subfigures.description: TEM/HAADF micrograph of a homogenized Fe–Mn–Al–C sample showing numerous bright cuboidal intragranular precipitates (κ-carbides) aligned along perpendicular directions within a darker matrix. White scale bar = 50 nm. No composition or condition label printed on the panel.

APT atom-map reconstruction of a needle-shaped specimen, colour legend Fe (grey), Al (cyan), Si (green), C (dark red); black scale bar = 20 nm. Cuboidal regions are enriched in Al, Si and C and depleted in Fe relative to the surrounding matrix.

Engineering stress (MPa) versus engineering strain (%) plot, y-axis 0–1200 MPa, x-axis 0–80%. Legend: 0Si (black circles), 1Si (red triangles), 2Si (blue squares). Strength increases and ductility decreases with Si content; the 2Si curve gives the highest stress but the shortest strain to failure.

3D APT reconstruction of a needle-shaped specimen with a blue–green–yellow colour scale representing C, labelled 'Cut' with an arrow, black scale bar = 25 nm. C-rich bands are visible along the specimen.

observations.observation: The top-left panel is a TEM/HAADF micrograph with a white scale bar of 50 nm, showing bright cuboidal precipitates aligned along orthogonal directions in a darker matrix.
The top-right panel is an atom-probe tomography atom map of a needle-shaped specimen with a colour legend reading Fe (grey), Al (cyan), Si (green), C (dark red) and a scale bar of 20 nm.
In the top-right APT map the cuboidal regions are co-enriched in Al, Si and C while the surrounding matrix is Fe-rich, i.e. the same cuboidal morphology as the TEM panel at a much finer scale.
The bottom-left panel plots engineering stress (MPa) against engineering strain (%) with y-axis ticks 0, 400, 800, 1200 and x-axis 0 to 80%.
The stress-strain legend identifies three curves by Si content: 0Si (black circles), 1Si (red triangles) and 2Si (blue squares).

The 2Si stress-strain curve attains a plateau above the 800 MPa gridline at very low strain and terminates abruptly at the lowest strain of the three, whereas the 0Si curve rises from near the 400 MPa level to its maximum at the highest strain (about 70-80%).
The bottom-right panel is a 3D APT reconstruction rendered with a blue-green-yellow colour scale for C, annotated 'Cut' with an arrow and a 25 nm scale bar.
The caption labels the figure 'Formation of κ-carbides in the homogenized state' and states it is reproduced with permission from reference [46], Copyright 2020, Elsevier.

The citing text states that κ-carbide formation in lightweight austenitic Fe–30Mn–9Al–1.2C steels is regulated by Si addition (0, 1, 2 mass%), which enhances Al and C activity according to thermodynamic calculations.

The citing text states that Si-free thermally treated steel contains ordered L1 nanodomains (<1 nm) with uniform element distribution, whereas 2 mass% Si produces cuboidal intragranular κ-carbides (L'1) averaging 11.5 nm with a volume fraction of 25.9% plus pronounced element segregation.
The citing text states that in the 2 mass% Si steel intergranular κ-carbides of 50-200 nm also form, and are more frequent during prolonged annealing than during aging.

The citing text states that κ-carbide precipitation raises yield strength from ≈450 MPa (0 mass% Si) to ≈950 MPa and increases strain hardening from 20% (0 mass% Si) to 55% and 83% at 1 and 2 mass% Si respectively.

The exact numerical endpoints of the stress-strain curves are not printed (only 0/400/800/1200 MPa and 0–80% tick marks)
